preamble: A direct change from a voiced postalveolar fricative [ʒ] to a voiceless aspirated retroflex affricate [ʈʂʰ] would require simultaneous devoicing, affrication, retroflexion and aspiration, and no clean case with a true [ʒ] source is documented. The closest attested pathway is the Middle Chinese 船 initial, reconstructed by most scholars as the voiced alveolo-palatal fricative [ʑ], which in level-tone syllables sometimes surfaces in Mandarin as aspirated [ʈʂʰ] and elsewhere as the fricative [ʂ]. The Middle Chinese 澄 initial previously cited here was a voiced retroflex stop [ɖ], not a fricative, so it does not illustrate this shift.

examples.note: 'Boat'. Baxter zywen; Zhengzhang /ʑiuᴇn/, Pan Wuyun /ʑʷiɛn/, Pulleyblank /ʑwian/; Li Rong, Wang Li and Karlgren instead reconstruct an affricate /d͡ʑ/. The source is alveolo-palatal [ʑ], not postalveolar [ʒ].
'Spirit'. Same 船 initial and level tone, but the reflex is the fricative [ʂ], showing that the affricated outcome is not regular.

sources: Baxter, W. H. (1992). A Handbook of Old Chinese Phonology. Mouton de Gruyter.
